ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 cancellation fee to the rider's original payment method and close the case; no driver violation or account flag is recorded, since the app recorded no cancellation reason and this clause (NS-3) carries no flag.
ruling.reasoning: The driver cancelled the trip at 22:41:35 [F4]. NS-0 first asks which clause applies, and it turns on the driver's reason for cancelling, which the app did not record — no reason was picked [F4]. His own words are therefore the record of why: at 22:41 he wrote "Sorry, tyre puncture, car got problem, have to cancel" [F11], and his written statement repeats "then my tyre went flat, so I had to cancel" [F14]. [NS-0]

element_findings.reason: No cancellation reason was picked in the app [F4], and the driver's only stated reason is his own car: 'Sorry, tyre puncture, car got problem, have to cancel' [F11], repeated in his statement 'then my tyre went flat, so I had to cancel' [F14]. Car trouble is expressly a reason of his own under NS-0, so the cancellation is not because the rider did not show: NS-1 does not hold and NS-3 applies, refunding the fee.

I read every chat message, the call-log line and the driver's statement [F10][F11][F13][F14]: they concern a pickup, a tyre puncture and an unanswered call. Nothing states or implies a threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous driving, so SAFE-1 is not engaged.

rejected_claims.reason: Conceded by the rider and settled by code: the GPS places the driver within 200 m from 22:35:30 and stationary 40 m away [F2][F3][F1], so NS-1(i) is met — but NS-1(i) is only one condition and does not decide the reason for cancelling.

Conceded and settled: arrival at 22:35:45 and cancellation 5 min 50 s later [F6][F7] exceeds the 5-minute free wait, so NS-1(ii) is met; that condition does not convert a car-trouble cancellation into a no-show cancellation.

Conceded: 2 in-app messages and 1 in-app call before cancelling [F5][F13] satisfy the attempt requirement of NS-1(iii), but the clause as a whole still requires that the driver cancelled because of the no-show.

Rejected: the argument that a tyre failure occurring after the wait is not 'a reason of his own' fails on the words of NS-0, which lists car trouble first among the driver's own reasons; the driver's own messages and statement supply exactly that reason [F11][F14].

Rejected: the $5.00 fee [F8][F4] is chargeable only on a driver cancellation for rider no-show under NS-1; where the driver's own words give his own reason, NS-3 applies and the fee is refunded, so the charge cannot stand.
